Structural analysis identifies a strong epitaxial effect, resulting in a giant compressive strain of ~4.16% at the interface that relaxes gradually toward the surface. The second-harmonic generation (SHG) signals might further reveal that such interfacial strain disrupted the inherent centro-symmetry of the cubic phase. SQUID magnetometry shows robust room-temperature ferromagnetism and clear magnetic anisotropy. Magneto-transport measurements reveal a robust AHE that remains stable at temperatures far exceeding room temperature. The scaling observed between the anomalous Hall resistance and longitudinal resistance strongly suggests that this effect is dominated by the intrinsic Berry curvature mechanism. Furthermore, density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the huge epitaxial strain induces band reconstructions and creates dense spin-orbit coupling gaps near the Fermi level, effectively doubling the anomalous Hall conductivity to match our experimental observations.

title: Framework to identify defect-insensitive electron transport in topological semimetals
abstract: Topological semimetals are of increasing interest to replace conventional metals for interconnects in future semiconductor chips, due to their potential to exhibit decreasing resistivity with reducing wire dimensions and a lower sensitivity to electron scattering at defects. First-principles evaluation of promising topological semimetals for interconnects typically employ non-equilibrium Green's functions (NEGF) techniques to estimate defect scattering, but such calculations for specific defect geometries are difficult to systematize and compare between disparate materials. Here, we develop an NEGF-based approach to systematically and rapidly evaluate the defect sensitivity of electron transport in materials without depending on material-specific defect geometries. Specifically, we analyze the eigen-spectrum of the transmission matrix for an incoherent ensemble of all-possible single-atom vacancy defects, which clearly reveals eigenvalues close to 1 for defect-insensitive transport modes. Applied to the leading candidates, we show that this robustness to defect scattering is extremely sensitive to surface orientation and Fermi level for each material. We find nearly-perfect insensitivity to defects only for wavevectors with single transport modes within specific Fermi level ranges in CoSi(001) and PtAl(001). Importantly, we also find high insensitivity for certain non-isolated modes in NbAs that emerge specifically due to spin-orbit coupling; these modes could not be identified previously as they were buried in the total transmission. These non-isolated modes have been buried in previous studies of total transmission, and can now be directly compared to other materials due to our standardization of defect-creation. This technique improves the state-of-the-art NEGF method and enables unbiased evaluation of future topological semimetal candidates for nanoscale interconnects.

title: Hierarchical Response Theory of Electronegativity from Atomic Mean Inner Potential
abstract: Electronegativity, introduced by Pauling nearly a century ago, remains chemistry's most widely used yet conceptually ambiguous quantity: is it a fixed atomic constant, or does it depend on chemical environment? We resolve this debate by recasting electronegativity as a continuous response function rooted in the Atomic Mean Inner Potential (AMIP), a quantum-mechanical observable accessible through first-principles calculation and, ultimately, electron holography. Expanding the AMIP with respect to fractional electron removal defines a hierarchy of physically distinct coefficients: the static electronegativity $χ_0$, the Electrostatic Rigidity $\mathcal{R}$---whose sign indicates whether an atom hardens or softens upon oxidation---and the Electrostatic Anharmonic Modulus $\mathcal{A}$. A logarithmic-derivative decomposition links these coefficients to two competing microscopic channels, electronic screening loss and geometric volume collapse, whose balance governs the response of all 102 elements. This competition produces a systematic dichotomy between softening main-group elements and hardening d-block elements, two scaling laws within the transition series (closed-shell stiffening and principal quantum softening), and two anomalies: a pronounced exchange-driven effect at half-filled d$^{5}$ configurations and a near-perfect cancellation in Ce. It also resolves the long-standing Cs--Fr controversy, identifying Fr as a critical element whose near-boundary response is amplified fivefold by relativistic contraction of the 7s orbital. The framework reproduces the classical Allen, Pauling, and Mulliken scales as well as Lewis acidity trends, and makes three falsifiable experimental predictions. It transforms electronegativity from a lookup-table number into a predictive, hierarchically structured quantum descriptor.

title: Intertwined complex orbital order and ferrimagnetism in honeycomb molybdate Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$
abstract: Motivated by the recent experimental interest in honeycomb molybdates A$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$, we return and develop the minimal models to capture the essential physics for Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$. It is pointed out that, the magnetism in these materials arises from the mutual induction between the spin-orbit coupling of the tetrahedral sublattice with active orbitals and the superexchange with the spins from the octahedral sublattice. Essentially, the superexchange between the tetrahedral and octahedral sublattices directly drives the ferrimagnetism, and the residual spin-orbit coupling on the tetrahedral sublattice induces the complex orbital order. The hybrid magnon-phonon excitations are further explored together with their resulting Berry curvatures and thermal Hall effect. We discuss the experimental relevance with Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$, and the framework can be extended to FeNiMo$_3$O$_8$, Ni$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$ and other isostructural magnets.

title: Superconducting parametric amplifiers based on arrays of unequal Josephson junction elements
abstract: Impedance matching is a crucial feature of an amplifier used to increase its instantaneous bandwidth and is typically achieved using static LC resonators. Here we show an approach to impedance matching in parametric amplifiers using arrays of unequal Josephson-junction-based elements (rf/dc SQUIDs, SNAILs, etc). The elements act either as small-footprint flux-tunable inductors forming an impedance-matching circuit, or 'active' amplifier elements which result in amplifier gain. We develop an analytical theory describing these systems, predicting a quasi-non-periodic amplifier frequency and gain modulation with applied flux and the broadening of gain bandwidths. We demonstrate this in devices using arrays of flux-focused SNAILs where flux biasing varies across the array. We find instantaneous bandwidths of 200 MHz with $>$17 dB of gain centred at $\sim$5.4 GHz in a device without a static impedance matcher. This broadening of amplifier bandwidth is stable with $>$100 MHz bandwidth at 17 dB gain across $>$1.2 GHz tunable bandwidth. Our analytical model captures flux dependence and qualitatively reproduces gain-bandwidths giving confidence in our understanding of these systems and allowing operational figures of merit to be optimised in future devices.

title: Consistent Modeling of SEI Growth via Electron Diffusion Validated Across Diverse Cell Specifications and Operating Conditions in LFP/Graphite Cells
abstract: Understanding and predicting degradation in lithium-ion batteries is critical for their widespread deployment. The continuous growth of the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) remains a dominant aging pathway, yet accurately modeling its kinetics across diverse cell specifications and operating conditions remains a significant challenge. Here, we present and validate a physically grounded SEI growth model mediated by the electron diffusion mechanism. This framework intrinsically captures the state of charge (SOC) dependence of degradation through the impact of the anode potential on the electron concentration, which governs the rate of SEI growth. The presented model explicitly accounts for variations in electrolyte salt, anode material, temperature, and cycling rate. Validation against experimental aging data for LFP/graphite cells demonstrates high predictive accuracy across a broad range of cell specifications and cycling conditions, including confined SOC windows, electrolyte salts (LiFSI, LiPF6), artificial graphites (AGC, AGD), temperatures (40-70°C), and C-rates (C/20-1C). Remarkably, a single, consistent set of parameters is applied to simulate the capacity fade for all experiments without recalibration. While quantitative overestimations occur during high-SOC storage periods, the framework consistently captures the observed degradation trends. Our findings underscore that lower SOC operation mitigates degradation, establishing a physics-based model for predicting long-term lithium-ion battery aging.

title: Zero-group-velocity modes in textured steel plates: experiments and elastic modeling
abstract: Zero-group-velocity (ZGV) resonances are investigated as a non-contact ultrasonic probe of elastic anisotropy in textured steel plates. Directional laser-ultrasonic measurements were performed on 70% cold-rolled Ti-stabilized interstitial-free steel plates in the full-hard and recrystallized condition. Experimental results were compared with predictions based on effective elastic stiffness tensors derived from X-ray diffraction measurements. Classical Voigt-Reuss-Hill estimates and microstructure-resolved finite-element homogenization reproduce the measured angular dependence of the ZGV frequencies well for both states, with the finite-element KUBC/SUBC bounds considerably narrower than the classical Voigt-Reuss bounds. For the full-hard state, agreement with the texture-based model is obtained only after a recovery treatment. This indicates that dislocations present in the full-hard material contribute to its elastic response, an interpretation that is further supported by theoretical estimations. An identifiability analysis shows that the directional ZGV measurements provide access to at least three independently observable combinations of the stiffness tensor components, and concluding suggestions for application in recrystallization monitoring are provided.

title: Compositional neural networks for multimodal X-ray and neutron scattering inversion
abstract: X-ray and neutron scattering are indispensable for structural characterization across condensed-matter physics and materials science. Yet, because scattering experiments generally record intensities without phase information, distinct structures can yield similar scattering patterns, rendering the corresponding inverse problems non-unique. This ambiguity can be reduced by combining complementary measurements, but their integration into machine-learning frameworks remains challenging. Here we introduce a modular framework for probabilistic multi-measurement analysis based on prior-amortized flow matching. Single-observation posterior estimators are trained separately for individual observation types or physical probes and combined only at inference time through a compositional sampler. This late fusion approach allows pretrained single-observation models to be reused without dedicated joint retraining. As a case in point, we consider reflectometry, which provides depth-resolved, nanometer-scale information about thin films and interfaces. Our single-observation demonstrations span X-ray, time-of-flight neutron and polarized neutron reflectometry. In separate co-refinement studies, task-matched estimators enable homogeneous composition across multiple neutron contrasts and heterogeneous multimodal composition of X-ray and neutron measurements. Together, these results establish compositional flow matching as a modular approach to uncertainty-aware inversion and co-refinement, with potential applicability to other scattering problems in which multiple observations constrain a common physical structure while retaining measurement-specific parameters.

title: Binder migration across film consolidation and pore emptying in electrode drying: a continuous model validated against drying-rate, thickness, and schedule experiments
abstract: Drying battery electrodes faster saves energy but drives dissolved binder toward the film surface, depleting the current-collector interface and weakening adhesion. Models of this migration stop convecting the binder when film consolidation ends, and models of the subsequent pore emptying omit the binder or start from an assumed binder field, so no simulation has followed binder convection through both stages that a drying schedule acts on. This study presents a continuous simulation of the dissolved binder field across both stages, driven by the published drying rates and completed by effective descriptions of the two questions the base transport physics leaves open: where the liquid of the consolidating film carries the binder, and when the binder stops moving as the pores empty. With a single parameter set, the simulation reproduces three types of published measurements: the change of the surface-to-interface binder ratio with drying rate over a factor of 5.6 and the surface and interface binder levels of films six times thicker; concentration profiles through the film interior; and the response of the interface binder to the time at which the drying rate is switched mid-process. Applied without further adjustment to a published three-stage schedule, the model reproduces the shortened drying and the full interface recovery when the rate is lowered early, and shows that its final high-rate stage begins after the binder has stopped. Combined with a coater-scale process model, the model can be used to identify operating points for electrode production that improve energy efficiency and product quality together.

title: Coupled Loop-within-Loop Resonators at the near-field: Extended Bandwidth and Short Pulse Response upon Parametric Conversion
abstract: Parametric frequency conversion have seen a renewed interest, specifically in superconducting quantum circuits at GHz range. These nonlinear convertors are typically narrow band and one may wish to extend their frequency range. Here, two coupled resonators are investigated: a loop-within-loop structure, whose gap is coupled by short, a diode, or simply left open. While simulations and experimental results are limited to GHz range, the concept is general. On their own, the loops exhibit natural frequencies of ca, f=1.5 GHz and f/2=0.73 GHz, respectively; the coupling modifies the resonance frequencies and increases its bandwidth. In one example, signal is fed from one loop and is received by the other. In another example, the input signal is provided across a coupling diode and is received by either loops. It is shown that in the case of nonlinear coupling, the frequency bandwidth can be as large as 3 GHz. Such bandwidth is associated with a very narrow temporal response of less than 150 ps, suggesting coherent effects through high-harmonic excitations at the near-field.

title: Comprehensive Acoustic Characterization of a Broadband Lateral MEMS Ultrasonic Transducer by Near-Field Acoustic Holography and Coupled Multiphysics Simulation
abstract: Broadband airborne ultrasonic transducers are attractive for applications such as ranging, echo-location, and acoustic material characterization, where wide bandwidths enable advanced excitation and signal-processing techniques. Recently, a lateral capacitive micromachined ultrasonic transducer (L-CMUT) employing electrostatically actuated in-plane microbeams was introduced as a broadband MEMS transducer concept. However, a comprehensive investigation of its acoustic radiation behavior and quantitative validation of corresponding multiphysics models have not yet been reported. In this work, we present a combined experimental and numerical characterization of a previously reported L-CMUT device operating between 10 kHz and 60 kHz. A coupled electrostatic--structural--thermoviscous finite-element model is combined with an acoustic boundary-element formulation to investigate the complete transduction chain from electrostatic actuation to acoustic radiation. The numerical predictions are validated experimentally using spherical near-field acoustic holography, enabling reconstruction of three-dimensional directivity patterns, radiated acoustic power, and spherical harmonic representations of the radiated sound field. The results show that the broadband behavior originates from strong thermoviscous damping within the narrow beam--stator cavities, resulting in strongly overdamped operation despite a mechanical eigenfrequency near 50 kHz. Good agreement between simulations and measurements is obtained for radiation patterns, radiated sound power, and spherical harmonic content. Furthermore, horn loading primarily redistributes acoustic energy and modifies directivity while only weakly affecting the total radiated acoustic power.

title: Continuously Tunable Mid-Infrared Metalens Integrating Moiré and Pancharatnam-Berry Phases
abstract: A varifocal mid-infrared metalens designed for focusing applications is proposed to integrate both Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) and Moiré pattern-based mechanisms for rotational wavefront control. The metalens employs two identical nanostructured discs featuring germanium (Ge) meta-atoms on calcium fluoride (CaF2) substrates, operating as birefringent half-wave retarders with 99.95% Polarization Conversion Ratio (PCR) and 83.65% total transmission power at 2 μm wavelength. Full-wave numerical simulations demonstrate continuous focal length tunability from 45 μm to 12 μm by rotating the second disk from 30 deg. to 120 deg., corresponding to the numerical aperture values ranging from 22.99% to 68.67%. The proposed metalens maintains reconfigurable focusing regardless of the incident light polarization, while concurrently enabling polarization-controlled operation via a phase-modulation mechanism that yields inverse responses under Right Circular Polarization (RCP) and Left Circular Polarization (LCP) illuminations.

title: Hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues in a finite temperature expanding free fermionic gas
abstract: A recent work considered the Page curve for entanglement entropy of a freely expanding one-dimensional Fermi gas starting from a finite box (the system) in a zero-temperature initial state that then expands in to a semi-infinite vacuum (the environment). For the case with a single defect at the system-environment junction, it was shown that the Yang-Yang entropy of the system computed from semiclassical hydrodynamics agrees with the microscopically computed entanglement entropy, yielding the Page curve. On the other hand, the environment Yang-Yang entropy showed a monotonic increase. Here, we propose a hydrodynamic description to obtain the eigenvalues of the microscopic correlation matrix for a nonzero temperature freely-expanding Fermi gas. For the system, the phase space density directly gives the correlation matrix eigenvalues and thus, via the Yang-Yang formula, yields the von-Neumann entropy. For the reservoir, a modification of the phase space density is required in the Yang-Yang formula, to incorporate coherences, in order to reproduce accurately the entropy. The hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues also leads to a Levitov-Lesovik type formula for the full-counting-statistics for a finite system in the transient regime. We provide a heuristic derivation of the correlation matrix eigenvalues based on a semiclassical wave-packet picture.

title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. I. Intrinsic errors and decoherence
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires quantum gates that combine short duration, high fidelity, and robustness to noise. As quantum processors scale, robustness becomes increasingly important because exhaustive characterization and frequent recalibration of individual gates become impractical. We present a comprehensive optimal-control framework for controlled-Z (CZ) gates between directly coupled, frequency-tunable transmons that systematically accounts for intrinsic Hamiltonian errors and realistic decoherence mechanisms, including energy relaxation and dephasing. Using smooth, single-shot flux pulses, we obtain 12-ns CZ gates---close to the theoretical speed limit of 11.6 ns---with intrinsic errors suppressed to the $2\times10^{-5}$ level. We construct dephasing noise models, calibrated against published experimental measurements, that capture fast dephasing from room-temperature control electronics and slow dephasing from $1/f$ flux noise. Using these models, we identify dephasing sweet spots that suppress sensitivity to dephasing noise. We further exploit transmon asymmetry as a design parameter to access distinct noise-resilient operating regimes. These results establish an experimentally applicable framework for balancing gate speed, fidelity, and noise robustness while reducing characterization and recalibration overhead.

title: From Traveling Waves to Synthetic Gauge Fields: A Field-Free Route to Superconducting Diode Effect
abstract: The superconducting diode effect requires the forward and reverse bias currents to differ, a scenario achieved via inversion and time-reversal symmetries broken together. The latter, and the more crucial one, is inevitably achieved by a magnetic field. Here, we show that a spatio-temporally driven chemical potential of the form, $μ_j(t)=μ+V\cos(ωt+\kd j)$, achieves both at once. Applied to a helical Shiba chain, the drive transmutes a traveling Peierls phase via generating an odd-in-momentum term, equivalent to an imaginary next-nearest-neighbour Haldane-like hopping in real space. Remarkably, the protocol is spin-blind, which renders the time-reversal breaking via a synthetic gauge flux rather than an effective Zeeman field. The rectification is odd in the drive wavevector, with exact zeros at $\kd=nπ$ and an analytical optimum at $\kd=2π/3$. It is however, even in the exchange coupling, $J$ and persists even at $J=0$. Furthermore, the rectification scales inversely with the pair-breaking gap, yielding approximately $50\%$ rectification in the topological phase and $10\%$ in the trivial phase. Symmetry breaking is thus drive-controlled, allowing it to be switched on, tuned, and reversed without an external magnetic field.

title: Electric-field tunable spin texture in dual-gated HfS$_2$/graphene van der Waals heterostructures
abstract: Spin-charge interconversion provides the essential link between spin information and electrical signals in spintronic devices. In spin-orbit coupled systems, spin-charge interconversion can contain multiple components associated with different spin-polarization directions, reflecting the underlying spin texture. Tuning this spin texture therefore provides a way to control not only the magnitude of spin-charge interconversion, but also the balance among its different components. Graphene-based van der Waals heterostructures provide an attractive platform for this purpose because interfacial spin-orbit coupling can host multiple spin-charge interconversion channels that couple to different spin-polarization directions. Here, we demonstrate electric-field control of spin texture in a dual-gated HfS$_2$/graphene van der Waals heterostructure, where independent control of carrier density and vertical electric field allows us to disentangle electrostatic doping from electric field-induced spin-orbit effects. Nonlocal spin precession measurements show that near zero vertical electric field, spin-charge interconversion is dominated by a spin Hall component with out-of-plane spins. Increasing the vertical electric field enhances additional in-plane spin components with Rashba-Edelstein-like character, including both parallel and perpendicular to the charge current contributions. These results provide experimental evidence that a vertical electric field can reconfigure the effective spin texture and control the corresponding spin-charge interconversion components, demonstrating electrical tunability of spin-orbit functionalities.

title: Effect of Annealing on Maze Domains in Topological Insulator - Magnetic Multilayer Heterostructures
abstract: Combining topological insulators with chiral magnetic multilayers offers the opportunity to greatly enhance the spin-orbit torque (SOT) driven manipulation of hosted spin textures, however this also exposes devices to the often poor temperature stability of the commonly used, Bi$_2$X$_3$-based (X is a chalcogenic element), topological insulator films. In this work we demonstrate through in-situ-annealing and polarised neutron reflectometry that the multilayer at a Bi$_2$Se$_3$ interface remains magnetically robust up to a temperature of 350 $^{\circ}$C: even as the Bi$_2$Se$_3$ epilayer structurally deteriorates. Through x-ray photoemission electron microscopy, an intermediate annealing temperature of $\sim$ 200 $^{\circ}$C was found to improve the domain ordering of the multilayer, allowing for field-induced skyrmion nucleation, all whilst sustaining minimal damage to the topological insulator

title: Interaction-Induced Bloch Geometry and Transverse Thermoelectric Transport
abstract: Electron--electron interactions can reconstruct Bloch wave functions, changing their geometry and the associated thermoelectric response. We derive the linear thermoelectric response within the Hartree--Fock (HF) approximation using the thermal length-gauge density-matrix approach, resolving Drude, symmetric quantum-metric, and antisymmetric Berry-curvature contributions. In a noninteracting Bloch eigenbasis, we separate the reconstructed Berry connection into the noninteracting connection and an interaction connection. This gives bare, coherence, and interaction-connection contributions to the anomalous thermoelectric response. We determine the constraints imposed by spatial inversion, rotational, time-reversal, and combined symmetries on the three transport channels. In the relaxation-time approximation, the leading weak-broadening behavior is $Γ^{-1}$ for the Drude contribution, $Γ$ for the quantum-metric contribution, and $Γ^0$ for the Berry-curvature contribution. The interband scalings apply away from band degeneracies. Self-consistent calculations for the triangular-lattice extended Hubbard model illustrate how interactions generate Berry curvature and a quantum metric, change the symmetry of the system, and thereby contribute to transverse thermoelectric transport.

title: Quantum Interference Enhanced Rectification in Mesoscopic Nanowires
abstract: Nanoscale nonreciprocal elements are needed to control signal flow in scalable quantum technologies, but existing nonreciprocal components are often bulky. Here, we show that a strongly nonreciprocal current-voltage relation can arise entirely from coherent elastic scattering in a mesoscopic Rashba nanowire with gate-defined scatterers. We first identify the symmetry constraints that enforce reciprocal transmission in a phase coherent conductor even when inversion and time-reversal symmetry are broken. We then show how gates that are capacitively coupled to the leads, together with a magnetic scatterer or transverse subband mixing, can remove these constraints. In the weak-scattering regime, nonreciprocal conductance originates from interference between distinct backscattering paths. In the strong-scattering regime, nonreciprocity can be resonantly enhanced by the hybridization of the transmitting channel with bound states that arise from a higher transverse subband or spin-split band. In this regime, we find that a bias-induced change in the gate potentials of about one percent can produce an order-unity diode response, i.e., electrons are transmitted almost as in a clean wire for one bias polarity, whereas for the other polarity the current is strongly suppressed.

title: Agentic World Action Models
abstract: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. Agentic robotics combines code-based planning and reasoning with reusable skills, but often lacks predictive grounding in physical dynamics. We introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction. We jointly model code, future video, and robot actions as three coupled generative streams within a unified mixture-of-transformers architecture. Within this architecture a code expert generates parameterized skill routines and control logic while video and action experts generate future visual states and low-level motor commands. Code serves two complementary roles: it structures multi-step prediction and control within the world model and represents skills as reusable programs for subsequent agentic execution. We further introduce an automated curation pipeline that labels robot and human video trajectories with aligned programs and consolidates recurring routines into reusable skill libraries. Evaluations on RoboTwin 2.0 and physical bimanual manipulation tasks show improved task performance over VLA and WAM baselines, alongside gains in language following, semantic reasoning and robustness, demonstrating that agentic code enables connection between planning, prediction and execution within WAMs.

title: CW-WAM: A Structured Contact-Wrench World Action Model for Force-Sensitive Manipulation
abstract: Force-sensitive manipulation requires contact and load information that is not provided explicitly by visual observations. We present CW-WAM, a world action model that jointly predicts video, motion, and contact wrench. Inspired by hybrid motion-force control, it contains a unified interaction module that treats both motion and contact wrench as modeling targets and predicts time-aligned motion-wrench chunks as control references. A pair-causal attention mechanism structures the motion-wrench dependencies, while a long fixed-length wrench memory retains past interaction information. The predicted wrench chunk acts as a force reference for a 20-Hz outer-loop admittance controller within a slow-fast control system that maintains force feedback and smooth motion between model queries. CW-WAM improves contact prediction and increases the insertion success rate from 25% to 70% for square pegs with 1-mm clearance per side and from 40% to 95% for power adapters, compared with WAM without wrench input. It also improves lifting-height accuracy across different loads. Our framework with an admittance controller reduces force-reference RMSE from 4.8 to 2.7 N for peg insertion and from 2.0 to 1.3 N for wiping, respectively, with smaller force fluctuations during successful execution. Project website: https://cw-wam-project.github.io/

title: Implementation of Dynamic Microsegmentation for a Multi-Robot Network
abstract: This report describes a laboratory instantiation of a dynamic microsegmentation function for an Internet-of-Things network, specifically a multi-robot network, using a commercial software-defined microsegmentation tool. Fine-grained dynamic segmentation policies are defined, where segments are adapted based on asset functional and health tags. Automated implementation of the dynamic policies in software is also undertaken. The microsegmentation solution is shown to automatically isolate an indicated threat in real time, while maintaining unaffected operations. The demonstration indicates that microsegmentation can be implemented in IoT networks, in a way that allows for robust operation in the face of threats and disruptions.

title: Machine Learning-Enabled Wireless Power Transfer: A Task-Oriented Review of Structural Optimization, State and Parameter Estimation, and Adaptive Control
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) systems must maintain efficient and safe energy delivery under variations in geometry, coupling, load, alignment, and operating conditions. Machine-learning methods are increasingly applied to accelerate structural design, estimate operating parameters and states, and support adaptive control and scheduling. This review develops a task-oriented framework organized around three interconnected domains: structural design and optimization, parameter and state estimation, and control and optimization. Supervised learning, reinforcement learning, and hybrid or physics-informed methods are compared in terms of data requirements, dependence on physical models, information sources, computational requirements, accuracy, online response, application scope, and optimization objectives. Supervised learning provides rapid surrogate modeling, regression, and classification when representative labeled data are available. Reinforcement learning addresses sequential control and scheduling but introduces challenges in reward design, safe exploration, and simulation-to-reality transfer. Hybrid methods integrate physical knowledge with data-driven models to improve data efficiency and physical consistency. The principal barriers to engineering deployment include limited and biased datasets, weak out-of-distribution generalization, insufficient physical consistency, unsafe online adaptation, embedded-resource constraints, and the absence of standardized benchmarks. Future research should prioritize uncertainty-aware and physics-informed learning, safe simulation-to-reality transfer, lightweight edge deployment, distributed coordination, reproducible evaluation, and digital-twin-assisted development.

title: Why the Swing Parameters Are Sloppy
abstract: Evangelou, Stanković, Kevrekidis and Transtrum compared analytic and data-driven assessments of parameter identifiability for the infinite-bus synchronous generator. Fisher information with the manifold boundary approximation method (MBAM), and output diffusion maps with geometric harmonics, report the same six identifiable parameters on the late window $t \in [3, 5]\text{ s}$, and both place the inertia $H$ and the damping $D$ among the unidentifiable ones. We explain this result from the geometry of the dynamics rather than from that of the parameter-to-data map. The rotor swing is a fast fibre that has collapsed onto a two-dimensional normally attracting invariant manifold (NAIM) of the transient fluxes before the window opens. The zeroth-order NAIM is exactly independent of $H$, $D$, $T_{d0}''$ and $T_{q0}''$, four of the five MBAM limits. We prove, under stated smoothness and rank conditions, that each of the four limits is a boundary of the model manifold at a distance equal, to first order in the parameter, to its current profiled speed. The same analysis predicts how identifiability changes with the experiment: neither a larger initial speed deviation nor a load change restores $H$ or $D$ in the late window, whereas the early window $[0, 2]\text{ s}$ makes $H$ the best-determined parameter. Evaluated in a physical metric fixed by synchrophasor accuracy limits, the late window identifies five parameters rather than six and the early window nine. The spiked-covariance structure of the linearised trajectory map explains why the principal components of whitened, sampled trajectories reproduce the prior-scaled Fisher spectrum, and regression on those components attains the Fisher-predicted recovery error in 113 of 114 parameter--scenario pairs.

title: Dual Effect and Certainty Equivalence Revisited for a Linear-Gaussian Dual Control Problem
abstract: This paper revisits the relation between dual effect and certainty equivalence (CE) through a scalar linear-Gaussian model. In dual control, the current input affects not only the immediate cost but also the information available for future decisions, and hence the future cost. Dynamic programming (DP) provides a natural framework for formulating dual control problems. At each step of the Bellman recursion, an optimal input minimizes the sum of the stage cost and the expected cost-to-go. We restrict attention to stage costs minimized by the CE input. However, CE may not minimize the Bellman objective because of the input-dependent expected cost-to-go. Classical no-dualeffect (NDE) conditions guarantee CE optimality in certain problem classes by requiring the conditional distribution of the estimation error to be independent of past controls. In the present model, we observe that CE can remain optimal at the level of a single Bellman recursion even when the classical NDE conditions fail, provided that the expected cost-to-go is independent of the current input. Motivated by this observation, we introduce a notion of NDE formulated directly at the level of the Bellman objective, which we call Bellman-side NDE. Under some mild regularity conditions, we show that Bellman-side NDE can be characterized by a heat equation. This characterization identifies the class of Bellman-side NDE functions, and further yields a decomposition of a generic cost-to-go function into a Bellman-side NDE component and a dual-effect component.

title: Seeking Cost--Effective Incentive for Merchant MTDC Investment in an AC Grid: A Parametric MISOCP Model to VSC Siting and Sizing
abstract: Deploying voltage source converter (VSC)-based multi-terminal DC (MTDC) networks in existing AC grids offers a promising solution for alleviating transmission congestion, enhancing power-transfer capability, and improving operational economy. However, constructing an MTDC network requires participation from merchant investors. Therefore, the transmission system operator (TSO) responsible for the AC grid must provide an adequate economic incentive that enables merchant investors not only to recover the MTDC investment cost but also to earn a reasonable return commensurate with their risk and expectations. An insufficient incentive may fail to attract merchant investment, whereas an excessive incentive may unnecessarily reduce the economic benefits retained by the TSO. Determining an appropriate incentive that balances these competing interests therefore becomes a critical issue. To address this issue, this paper formulates a sharing-rate-parameterized mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) model that jointly optimizes VSC siting and sizing while coordinating AC/DC system operation. A straightforward search procedure is then employed to identify the benefit-sharing rate that meets the investor's expectations while preserving sufficient benefits for the TSO. Case studies demonstrate the operating-cost benefits of MTDC integration and validate the proposed search strategy for seeking such a benefit-sharing rate.

title: Parallel AI Agent Collaboration as Graph-Structured Distributed Block Optimization
abstract: Parallel AI agents can produce useful local edits yet degrade a shared solution when their edits are combined. We model this coordination problem as discrete block optimization with an exactly evaluable objective and a known dependency graph. Independent sets certify compatible edits whose verified gains, measured against the same current solution, add exactly. A coordinator constructs a safe compatible candidate and can also evaluate interacting edits to capture favorable interactions. We prove that an optimal fractional coloring yields a merger that preserves a $1/χ_f(G)$ fraction of the total verified local improvement, where $χ_f(G)$ is the graph's fractional chromatic number. This guarantee is tight among mergers that select a subset of the same proposals. Under conditional local-improvement guarantees and a block error-bound condition, repeated collaboration converges geometrically in the objective gap. The rate separates task structure, agent allocation, and computation cost, yielding a linear program for agent assignment and an explicit time-cost trade-off. Code-repair experiments show that verified merging resolves conflicts between individually useful edits that cause naive merging to fail. On larger conflict-free tasks, parallel agents reduce modeled completion time at higher input-token-equivalent cost. On three public road networks, fractional integration retains 922 units of verified graph-cut improvement across 90 paired runs. For route-search agents sharing exclusive access to vehicle routes, fractional scheduling reduces measured wall time by a median of 15% across twelve paired runs, with route-cost changes varying across runs.

title: Facets of the X-ray polytope of doubly stochastic matrices
abstract: We study the polytope of anti-diagonal X-rays of k x k doubly stochastic matrices, the image of the Birkhoff polytope under the map that sums the entries along each anti-diagonal. Its facets other than the coordinate facets are the minimal joint tail bounds for lattice laws of a sum of two dependent uniform random variables. We give an exact facet criterion in terms of the allowed edges of a tight graph. For rays of the underlying tropical fan, total support of the tight graph suffices for a facet but is not necessary, as an example with k=19 shows. Up to affine functions and positive scaling, the potentials that define a facet form a polytope whose vertices are its rays. Facets propagate by padding and by grid refinement under explicit hypotheses. We give infinite families of facets from no step potential, facets of quadratic height, superpolynomially many facets, and a classification of three-step potentials. Total support of a step potential is characterized by a Hall-type condition on block starts; with computer assistance, total support decides facets of step potentials for k<=26. The facet counts up to k=12 are found directly for k<=3 and, for k>=4, come from an enumeration by a provably complete algorithm; an independent exact recomputation reproduces its ray lists for 5<=k<=12.

title: DiffVortex: A quantum-inspired fast solver for incompressible flows
abstract: Matrix-product-state (MPS) and quantized tensor-train (QTT) representations offer a promising framework for computational fluid dynamics, with logarithmic run time and memory scaling in mesh size when bond dimensions remain bounded. Existing MPS-based solvers are Eulerian: they compress velocity fields and enforce immersed-body boundary conditions through static masks or body-fitted coordinates. Moving or flexible bodies complicate this approach: deformation requires updating MPS masks every time step, while filamentary vorticity in high-Reynolds-number flows may resist low-rank compression. We propose a complementary approach: compress the Biot--Savart kernel rather than the flow state, evolve vorticity using Lagrangian vortex particles, and represent immersed bodies by bound vortex sheets on Lagrangian surface points. Our main theoretical result is a lifting theorem: QTT rank $r$ of the kernel implies matrix-product-operator (MPO) rank at most $2^d r$ for the corresponding convolution operator in $d$ dimensions, independent of grid resolution. This bound is sharp for our interleaved ordering. With quantics tensor cross interpolation, the moment-to-local stage of a single-level fast multipole method becomes a precomputed tensor-network contraction with quasi-linear complexity, retaining Lagrangian flexibility for immersed bodies. Our PyTorch implementation (\texttt{DiffVortex}) is end-to-end differentiable, runs on GPUs, and handles $6.7\times10^{7}$ particles on a single device. We validate against reference vortex-method results for an impulsively started cylinder and exact and reference solutions for inviscid elliptical vortices. We also demonstrate two-dimensional flows past rigidly moving, multiple, and deforming bodies, including gradients propagated through the full time integration.

title: Acoustic control of Rayleigh-regime liquid-jet breakup using a through-hole MHz transducer
abstract: This experimental study demonstrates MHz-order acoustic control of Rayleigh-regime liquid-jet breakup using a compact through-hole lithium niobate thickness-mode transducer integrated at the nozzle exit and driven near its 6.7 MHz resonance. Jet dynamics were measured by high-speed shadowgraphy at 50,000 fps, and breakup lengths were obtained from instantaneous jet-length records using an autocorrelation-based method that identifies statistically separated breakup events. Acoustic actuation produced visible interfacial corrugations and reduced the normalized breakup length, $L_b/d$, for both water and glycerol--water jets. In water, the response was threshold-like at low Weber number and weakened as the jet velocity increased to We ~ 50. A reduced-order threshold correlation, fit to the water amplitude and velocity sweeps, captured this abrupt shortening and the subsequent loss of actuation efficacy. More viscous glycerol--water mixtures shortened immediately at low forcing, indicating a distinct acoustic-coupling regime rather than a universal collapse of the water response. A wetting-control experiment showed that liquid spreading at the nozzle base can also shorten the jet, so the measured response reflects coupled radiation-pressure forcing, capillary-wave feedback, and wetting-mediated disturbance injection. Resolved droplet tracking further showed that MHz excitation changes the visible gate-crossing droplet population, although sub-resolution mist and micron-scale atomization were not measured. These results establish through-hole MHz actuation as a compact route for modifying free-surface jet breakup and provide a repeatable image-analysis protocol for experimental-fluid-mechanics measurements.

title: Swarmlet: a GPU-resident reformulated vortex particle method for coupled multirotor aerodynamics and flight dynamics
abstract: We present Swarmlet, a GPU solver for the unsteady aerodynamics and flight dynamics of one or many multirotor vehicles. The wake is a meshless, evolving-core vortex particle field in the reformulated (rVPM) large-eddy formulation, coupled to rotor models of three fidelities, six-degree-of-freedom vehicles and flight control. Particles carry a smooth core of compact support whose field outside four core radii is exactly the singular Biot-Savart field, so the multipole far field of the treecode carries no regularization error. The subfilter closure is a dynamic eddy viscosity on a fixed filter width, applied by core spreading with a Lagrangian exchange of its local excess under an explicit stability bound, and the strengths are relaxed by projection; global corrections make both the exchange and the relaxation conserve total vorticity and linear impulse. All rotor models shed connected bound circulation, the disks along the arcs swept in each step however long, so the wake receives the lift impulse. The solver agrees with direct summation to $5\times 10^{-7}$ and converges at third order in time. Without calibration, an actuator-line model that includes its own near sheet predicts the hover thrust of a DJI 9443 propeller within 2%. With calibrated section polars it reproduces a Crazyflie propeller's thrust and torque within 3.2% at three speeds and the near wake of a hovering quadrotor with relative $L^2$ differences of 0.08-0.21 against particle image velocimetry, while the wake keeps the delivered impulse. A closed-loop formation of 100 quadrotors, run at a coarser setting on one GPU, illustrates the coupled method at swarm scale.

title: Automated Discovery of Physically Interpretable Subgrid Length Scales for Detached Eddy Simulation via Agentic AI
abstract: Traditional turbulence-model development relies heavily on expert knowledge and is time-consuming. This study develops an agentic AI framework, DEScover (automated Discovery of DES closures), to explore subgrid length scales for detached eddy simulation (DES). The user provides only a modeling idea: the length scale is the grid width normal to the local vortex axis. Four large language model (LLM) agents then propose, review, implement, and evaluate candidate formulations and generate scripts for CFD simulations. The Discovery Agent infers the vortex axis from various vortex-identification methods. The candidates are tested on four cases spanning canonical and engineering flows: a flat plate, a backward-facing step, a free shear layer, and an iced airfoil. For all test cases, the best candidate consistently outperforms the standard length scale based on the maximum cell size. Its accuracy is similar to, or slightly better than, that of the expert-designed shear-layer-adapted length scale. Each agentic discovery run takes about 25 minutes on average, excluding the CFD simulations. These results show that LLM-based reasoning can significantly accelerate the discovery of physically interpretable turbulence models and reduce reliance on manual expert formulation.

title: Hydrodynamics of microalgae in sea spray
abstract: Airborne transmission of biological matter is likely to cause numerous respiratory distress in coastal populations during certain harmful algal blooms. While we know that dissolved algal toxins aerosolize, the contribution of particle-associated toxins is still unknown. The observation of microalgae in the atmosphere suggests that cells or cell debris could be a carrier. Exchange of particulate matter between ocean and atmosphere is driven by sea spray: microplastics and bacteria aerosolize in jet droplets, following the bursting of air bubbles. However, current models for particle capture only consider surface effects, which fail to explain how large microalgal cells (5-50 um) can be entrapped in jet drops (100-800 um). Here, we demonstrate with a variety of species that microalgae are consistently captured in jet drops, and derive a new particle capture model based on the hydrodynamics of the jet. Using the enrichment factor, which measures the increase in concentration in the first jet drop relative to the bulk, we uncover two regimes. The transition between regimes strongly depends on cell size. In addition, we highlight the dynamics of particles within the jet and derive an enrichment model based on hydrodynamics rather than surface considerations. This work widens and generalizes established results on bacterial and microplastic entrapment in jet drops, resolving discrepancies found in the literature. Finally, we demonstrate that sea spray can aerosolize toxic Ostreopsis cf. ovata cells. This reveals a potential particulate pathway for airborne toxicity during harmful algal blooms and raises the question of the relative contribution of particles to that of dissolved toxins.

title: Auditing LLM Alpha-Factor Mining: Metric Provenance and Full-Cohort Reanalysis
abstract: Reliable evaluation of LLM-based alpha mining requires more than positive backtest summaries. We audit a preserved project at three levels: historical run counters, outcome retention, and a separately scoped public reanalysis. Three historical runs report 67, 20, and 11 keep decisions, but the comparison mixes metric populations: a mean over kept candidates is compared with a mean of per-round maxima, and successful evaluations with all returned outcomes. These artifacts cannot identify an architecture advantage. A released 1,837-expression catalog also excludes non-positive OOS outcomes, making its zero-reversal rate non-informative. We then account for all 1,047 unique expressions in a frozen, IS-screened preserved pool using forty A-shares and 2024-2025 rank associations. A versioned public-operator correction yields 923 scorable records, 99 with insufficient valid dates, and 25 unsupported, without modifying the other 990 prior diagnostics. Among scorable records, 671 have positive and 252 negative signed mean rank-IC. Simple untrained references also show positive associations, so this distribution does not establish incremental agent skill or profitability. The case study motivates explicit metric grains, immutable cohort accounting, and provenance-aware interpretation rather than architectural rankings from incomplete records.

title: Inconsistency in the analytic hierarchy process under data uncertainties
abstract: In this paper, we study the inconsistency of matrices in multicriteria group decision making under the assumption of uncertainty in their entries. The study binds together an $n$-dimensional probabilistic product measure $P$ and the Koczkodaj indicator $K_{n}$ of order $n$ used in pairwise comparisons. In the case of $n$ greater than 3, it starts with a new definition of $K_{n}$ based on the Steiner triple system of order $n$. It is of interest that the new indicator requires only $O \left( n ^{2} \right)$ evaluations, while the old one $O \left( n ^{3} \right)$. Our study results in analytic formulae for the probabilities of events $K_{n} \leq \varepsilon$ corresponding to uniform, exponential, and normal distribution functions, whenever the remainder of $n$ divided by 6 equals 1 or 3. For the remaining values of $n$, we present analytic formulae for their strict bounds. The formulae lead to much more efficient algorithms when compared with Monte Carlo simulations. This unexpected feature is illustrated by a few numerical experiments.

title: An Eco-Friendly Tourism Trip Planner Driven by Z-Number Uncertainty: Evidence from Baku, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Tashkent, and Istanbul
abstract: Deployed tourism trip planners ingest travel times and ratings as exact numbers, although routing services return travel times that vary with the hour of departure and a platform rating may rest on a handful of reviews or on tens of thousands. We present an eco-friendly trip planner that represents both quantities as Z-numbers, which pair a fuzzy restriction on a value with a fuzzy reliability on the evidence behind it, and that constructs them directly from routing-service observations at six departure hours and from platform review counts rather than from linguistic elicitation. A hybrid loss combines score, carbon, travel-time, and reliability terms, and an adaptive large neighborhood search returns single-day itineraries with per-leg reliability annotations through a conversational front end. We compare the planner with a crisp-mean baseline under an identical optimizer in Baku, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Tashkent, and Istanbul, with fifteen points of interest and thirty seeds per city, and we evaluate the selected itineraries on their trip carbon and their total travel time. Pooled over 150 seed-paired runs, the planner lowers trip carbon from 3.24 to 2.61 kg (19.3%, Wilcoxon p = 0.017; city-clustered bootstrap interval 6.4% to 26.7%) and travel time from 123 to 109 minutes per trip (11.5%, p = 2.8e-10; interval 5.0% to 18.2%). The travel-time reductions survive a Holm correction in Baku, Istanbul, and Abu Dhabi, the carbon reduction is significant in Baku and large but uncertain in the dispersed catalogs of Dubai and Abu Dhabi, and neither metric changes in Tashkent. Review counts were measured for Baku and estimated for the other four cities, and the comparison involves a single baseline, so the results establish feasibility and direction rather than a general advantage. Code, routing caches, frozen routing tables, and per-seed results are openly released.
